title: JavaScript arrays

inventory.title: Array constructor, static methods and static property

scopeExclusions: Array-like objects not inheriting from Array
accuracyFacts: An Array is an exotic object with special handling for array-index property keys. Its length is a non-enumerable, non-configurable data property initially writable, with value from 0 through 2^32 - 1. Assignment applies array-length conversion and range rules. Shrinking deletes configurable own indexed properties; if a non-configurable index blocks deletion, length is restored to one greater than that index and the requested operation fails.
An array index is not the same as every canonical-looking numeric string; 2^32 - 1 is not an array index. Adding an own array-index property at or above length updates length to index + 1.

Array(n) with one Number argument creates an array with that length and holes, while Array.of(n) creates a one-element array containing n. Array.from prefers an iterable and otherwise reads an array-like length and indexed values.

Array.fromAsync is standardized in ECMAScript 2024. It prefers an async iterator, then adapts a synchronous iterator, and otherwise consumes array-like indexed values. Mapper results are awaited sequentially in every path. It awaits source values from the synchronous-iterator adapter and array-like path; a value yielded by a genuine async iterator is passed through without an additional Await by Array.fromAsync (though async-generator semantics may themselves await yielded Promises).

A hole is an absent indexed property, not a stored undefined value. Whether a method skips holes, visits them as undefined, or preserves/creates holes differs by method and must be explained per operation.

Methods such as forEach, map, filter, some, every, reduce, and indexOf test property presence before reading an index; inherited indexed properties can count as present. Methods such as find/findIndex/findLast/findLastIndex and includes read each index; when neither the array nor its prototype chain has that index, the read produces undefined.

Array.from over a sparse Array uses its iterator, whose values at holes are undefined, so the result is dense. Array-like Array.from and Array.fromAsync read each index up to length and likewise produce values for absent indices.
Array iterators are live with respect to the iterated Array: each next step uses the current length and gets the current indexed value, so mutations during iteration can affect later results.

concat, slice, splice, map, filter, flat, and flatMap use species-related construction where specified; the ECMAScript 2023 copying methods toReversed, toSorted, toSpliced, and with create ordinary Arrays rather than consulting Array species.

The default sort order compares string representations by UTF-16 code units. A comparator must define a consistent ordering for predictable results; sort is stable in current ECMAScript, while its time and space complexity are not specified. Comparator results are converted to Number and NaN is treated like zero.

The copying methods toReversed, toSorted, toSpliced, and with do not mutate the receiver and create dense results by reading indexed positions; holes therefore become undefined values. Their names describe the changed copy, while reverse, sort, and splice mutate the receiver.

Array.prototype methods are generally generic over array-like receivers unless their algorithm requires otherwise; generic use requires a length and indexed properties, but the full design of standalone array-like objects is outside this topic.

Array.prototype[Symbol.unscopables] initially lists at, copyWithin, entries, fill, find, findIndex, findLast, findLastIndex, flat, flatMap, includes, keys, toReversed, toSorted, toSpliced, and values as true; it affects with-statement binding resolution only, not ordinary property lookup. Its symbol property on Array.prototype is non-writable, non-enumerable, and configurable.

Array.prototype.toLocaleString forwards locale/options to element conversions, while the separator between elements is implementation-defined and locale-sensitive; those arguments do not select that separator.
